Compared list scheduling with exact enumerated optima throughout the independently recorded finite exhaustive domain.

evidence: Re-derived P-p_j >= mS_j and C_max <= P/m + (1-1/m)p_j from least-load assignment of the last-finishing job.
Substituted the independent lower bounds P/m <= OPT and p_j <= OPT to obtain the (2-1/m) competitive ratio.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The derivation is not transferred to unknown sizes, nonidentical or ineligible machines, setup, release-time queueing, deadlines, or other objectives.

evidence: Checked one machine, zero-size work, invalid zero machines, tied least loads, a tight adversarial order, and a persistently overloaded service.
Checked eligibility failure, unknown size, prediction underestimation, preemption cost, retry duplication, cancellation races, starvation, capacity loss, and feedback-sensitive arrivals.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: EDF scope, Little's-law prerequisites, and stability claims are explicitly conditional rather than universal.

evidence: Checked conservation of assigned load, exactly one assignment per job, deterministic tie breaking, nonnegative remaining work, eligibility, and common comparator resources.
Checked logical job identity, fenced retries, timestamp ordering, charged transition costs, overload fallback, and reconstruction telemetry.
invariant_checking.notes: Work conservation is subordinate to declared feasibility, reservation, safety, fairness, and overload policy.

evidence: Reviewed the list-scheduling last-job proof for premise use, lower-bound direction, the m=1 boundary, and zero-size jobs.
Reviewed the EDF exchange statement and confined it to the classical independent-job, one-processor, preemptive feasibility model.
proof_review.notes: The EDF paragraph states its exchange structure without extending optimality to multiprocessor, nonpreemptive, setup, overload, or value models.

evidence: Audited optimal, feasibility-optimal, competitive, tight, lower-bound, necessary, sufficient, causal, empirical, exact, and independently checked language.
Separated mathematical model, theorem, proof argument, implementation mechanism, prediction, operational policy, and observed evidence.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No trace result, simulator, shadow comparison, or local execution is presented as a universal scheduling guarantee.

evidence: The CPython 3.14.4 snippet exited zero with exact assignments, loads, makespans, tight ratio, zero-size behavior, and invalid-machine rejection on macOS 13.7.8 x86_64.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Execution supports the tested implementation and finite domain only; it does not establish production latency, stability, fairness, safety, or feedback behavior.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed information and action protocols, objectives, list scheduling, deadline feasibility, non-clairvoyance, overload, fairness, failures, predictions, evaluation, and guarantee boundaries.

pedagogical_review.notes: The Level-II chapter derives its central guarantee, contrasts incompatible scheduling models, supplies ten distinct analytical and operational examples, and ends with five progressive exercises and complete answers.

limitations: Internal source, mathematical, snippet, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical review only; no external academic, real-time-systems, operating-system, platform, distributed-systems, safety, clinical, performance, or operational review is claimed. Formal guarantees remain limited to their stated machine, information, action, and objective models; production conclusions remain conditional on workload, estimator, implementation, resource, feedback, and failure assumptions.
